title: paged-kv-cache: block allocator reuse + locality-aware pinning optimizations
author: Priya Menon
description: Motivation: The paged KV cache has been suffering from allocation churn and cross-stream eviction noise under mixed-length workloads and heavy continuous batching. This causes increased tail latency and unnecessary GPU memory copies. What this PR does (single-string description): - Replace monolithic block allocation strategy with a size-class-aware allocator that bins blocks by power-of-two sizes. This reduces fragmentation and speeds up allocation paths. - Add a reuse pool for recently freed blocks keyed by (size-class, device-locality) to favor reuse on the same GPU/socket. Reuse pool is lock-free for hot-paths and fallback-protected for cold paths. - Locality-aware pinning: extend pinning metadata to include a locality tag (NUMA/socket/GPU-id). Pinning now prefers blocks pinned to request locality and falls back to least-recently-used across locality groups. - Reference-counted pinning + soft-ttl: pins increment a lightweight refcount and use a configurable soft TTL to allow eventual eviction for long-lived inactive keys. - Add metrics and traces for allocation hit/miss, reuse-rate, pin evictions, and locality affinity. - Safety: added bounds checks, additional unit tests, and a GC pass that validates refcounts on background threads. Compatibility and rollout plan: - Implementation is behind config flag `paged_kv.block_optimizer_v2` and defaults to off for canary nodes. - Added a smoke integration test that runs continuous-batching workload locally. - Incremental rollout: start canary with 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% if metrics are green. Benchmarks / Results (summary): - Mixed-length chat workload (seq len distribution 16/64/512): end-to-end token throughput +8-12% on p3/rtx-class machines. - Eviction churn (measured as evicted blocks/sec) down ~25% in high-concurrency tests. - 99th percentile latency improved by ~6-10ms for heavy batching scenarios. Notes and follow-ups: - We should instrument scheduler to be able to prefer locality-aligned batching (follow-up ENG-4780). - Consider exposing soft-ttl as a tuning knob per-customer for Dedicated deployments. Checklist: - [x] Unit tests for allocator and pinning semantics - [x] Integration smoke test with continuous batching harness - [x] Benchmarks and dashboard panels added - [x] Feature flag guarded for staged rollout

perf(paged-kv): locality-aware pinning and soft-ttl refcounting

review_comments: Ben Carter: Left a couple of comments on the concurrency path — prefer lighter-weight atomics for the hot path to reduce cacheline contention.
Priya Menon: Addressed in second commit: replaced the mutex fallback with a per-shard spin-lock and added comments explaining the contention tradeoff.
Asha Rao: Can we add a short-circuit to avoid reuse pool lookups for tiny allocations (<= 64B)? Suggested micro-optimizations added.
Diego Morales: Verified benchmark harness and asked to include p99 latency panel. Added dashboard and CI perf workflow.
Ben Carter: Approving after verifying unit tests and perf numbers on canary instance.
release_notes: Paged KV cache: improved block allocator with size-class reuse pool and locality-aware pinning. Expected improvements: 8-12% throughput, reduced eviction churn, lower tail latency. Rollout behind feature flag.
